text:
Maya: noticed huge churn in eu cluster, spot nodepool gpu-spot-eu exhausted and scheduler spamming scale-up. pods in Pending with 'Insufficient GPUs' 
Omar: saw the same, autoscaler events are showing repeated AddNodes for gpu-spot-eu then immediate Terminate events from cloud (spot reclaim) :grimacing: 
sre-bot: autoscaler event stream: 
  - 2026-03-18T09:12:10Z CA: scale-up request for nodegroup=gpu-spot-eu desired=32 current=4 (reason: 120 pending pods)
  - 2026-03-18T09:12:32Z cloud: spot instance interruption for nodegroup=gpu-spot-eu (terminated 12 instances)
Jin: quick check - pending pods all part of nightly batched-inference job-rt, nodeSelector: gpu-type: ampere-v2. Nodepool label is gpu-type: ga104 on a few nodes, looks like new job used wrong label and admission mutated it? 
Lia: ugh, I saw a recent rollout to batch-runner that changed nodeSelector in a configmap -> probably propagated to cronjob template.
Maya: commands I ran: 
```
kubectl get pods -n infra -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Pending
kubectl describe pod batch-run-2026-03-18-xxx -n infra
kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-spot-eu --show-labels
```
Omar: output showed 95% of pending pods have affinity to gpu-type=ampere-v2 but almost all spot nodes are labeled gpu-type=ga104 -> scheduler can't place, CA starts scaling other pools to compensate and ends up spinning.
Jin: immediate mitigation plan: 1) Stop scheduling more batch jobs (pause cronjob). 2) Add taint to spot nodes so CA won't try to place mislabelled pods there. 3) Bump gpu-dedicated-eu temporarily to absorb backlog.
Lia: pausing cronjob now: `kubectl scale cronjob batch-runner -n infra --replicas=0` :white_check_mark:
Maya: taint applied to spot nodes: `kubectl taint nodes -l pool=gpu-spot-eu spot-evict=true:NoSchedule` -> prevents further scheduling while we sort labels.
Omar: requested infra to raise gpu-dedicated-eu desired from 2 -> 6 to soak pending jobs, infra confirmed and started provisioning on-demand.
sre-bot: deploy-bot noted autoscaler config changes: recent CA filter for nodegroup tag 'preferred=true' missing; CA now treats spot pool as generic and aggressively scales.
Deploy-bot: last deployment that touched cronjob config: build/registry:batch-runner@sha256:abcd1234 by Pipelines CI at 2026-03-18T08:55:00Z. Reverted that rollout to previous image to remove wrong nodeSelector.
Jin: after revert, updated cronjob template in k8s to explicitly set nodeSelector: 
```
nodeSelector:
  gpu-type: ga104
```
and added tolerations for dedicated pool if needed.
Maya: started rolling drain of mis-labelled spot nodes into cordoned state so they won't pick up new pods: `kubectl cordon <node>` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets` for a few at a time.
Lia: observed scale-down suppression is required while we stabilize. Patch CA configmap to increase scaleDownDelay to 10m and set expander to least-waste to avoid overprovisioning.
Omar: cost note: on-call approved temporary on-demand bump, estimate +$6k/day if sustained. Will track in incident cost channel.
Jin: root cause hypothesis: CI rollout accidentally replaced a templated nodeSelector variable with 'ampere-v2' default; combined with missing CA label filter and high concurrency of cronjobs led to repeated CA scale-up + spot interruptions -> thundering fallback -> evictions.
Maya: current state summary: cronjob paused, spot pool tainted/cordoned, dedicated pool scaled up and taking traffic, backlog draining (approx 800 pods pending -> 230 now), autoscaler config patched for conservative behavior.
Lia: add follow-ups: 1) admission webhook to validate nodeSelector values for gpu workloads. 2) CA config: add nodegroup tag filter to ignore spot for certain labels. 3) adjust cronjob concurrency and backoff. 4) runbook update for spot reclaim + CA interaction.
Omar: creating P1 incident ticket and paging HW on-call for post-mortem. I added alert: high CA add/remove rate > 5/min.
Maya: thanks all, I'll keep monitoring. If backlog doesn't clear in 30m we'll keep dedicated pool at bumped capacity and schedule a retro. :thumbsup:
